summary: Elevated initial-output latency for chat completions after quantized runtime cutover
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a significant increase in time before the assistant emits the first chunk of text (initial-output latency) for chat completion API calls following our 2026-03-09 cutover to a quantized runtime and new kernel selection logic. Impact: Multiple production endpoints for LexiDocs experienced time-to-first-output increases from ~120ms to 1.8-3.2s for short-chat prompts, causing errors in their synchronous UI and several user-facing timeouts.
impact: Several hundred chat requests per minute affected for the customer; real user experience degraded (UI spinner timeouts); incident causing SLA alert to trigger for enterprise contract.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use LexiDocs customer API key bound to model redwood-v2-chat-small-quant.
2) Send a minimal chat completion via /v1/chat/completions with max_tokens=64 and streaming disabled.
3) Measure time from POST to first non-empty response chunk.
4) Repeat across multiple warm and cold connections; compare against runtime pinned to 2.0.1 (pre-cutover).
logs:
Representative request log: request_id=rid-20260310-9ab3; route=/v1/chat/completions; model=redwood-v2-chat-small-quant; runtime=runtime-quant-2.4; kernel=auto-select; t_request_received=11:22:03.102Z; t_first_output=11:22:06.412Z; backend_5xx=false; backend_latency=3.31s.
Router note: observed high scheduling delay for 80% of samples. KV-cache-warmup shows cache-miss on first seg for pinned sessions.
comments:
2026-03-10 | Ava Martinez (Support): Initial report received from LexiDocs at 11:40 UTC. Customer observed UI timeouts after routine deploy. Attached request IDs and screenshots.
Action: Escalated to on-call SRE and assigned to Samira.

2026-03-10 | Samira Patel (SRE): Confirmed elevated median initial-output latency in us-east-1 for redwood-v2-chat-small-quant after runtime cutover. Reproduced locally against production routing. Opening kernel-selector investigation.
Next: revert customer routing to pre-cutover runtime as temporary mitigation.

2026-03-10 | Engineering (runtime): Noted that new kernel-selection heuristics choose a quantized int4 kernel that has a larger setup cost for short prompts due to extra prefetch and per-shard compilation path. Hypothesis: setup overhead dominating for <64-token chat turns.

2026-03-11 | Samira Patel (SRE): Performed targeted rollback of LexiDocs routing to runtime-2.0.1 at 02:10 UTC. Customer reports immediate reduction in initial-output latency to ~140ms. Will keep routing pinned while kernel-selector patch is developed.
investigation_notes:
Observed pattern: long scheduler wait + kernel setup time. Cold KV cache misses amplified by kernel prefetch step in quantized path.
Heap/profile dump: increased cpu spin-up and shader compile time for int4 kernels on small sequences.

A/B test: routing 10% of traffic to runtime-2.0.1 vs runtime-quant-2.4 shows 92% lower median initial-output latency on 2.0.1 for short prompts. For long prompts (>512 tokens) quantized runtime still shows cost benefits with comparable throughput.

Trace snapshot: https://traces.redwood/trace/abc123 shows per-request timeline: accept -> assign-slot (80-150ms) -> kernel-setup (900-1200ms) -> execution (10-30ms) -> first-output. Kernel-setup dominates.

Hypotheses: (1) kernel-selection now triggers a per-model JIT or codegen for quantized kernels on first use; (2) heuristic incorrectly selects int4 kernel for small batches where int8 or fp16 would be faster; (3) router affinity changes increased cold-start frequency for this customer's pods.
Logs cross-ref: see incident timeline in Slack #incidents (thread: quant-cutover-2026-03-09) and infra PR notes.
Priority: fix kernel-selection heuristics to avoid heavy setup for short sequences OR add runtime flag that opts out of JIT/codegen for small-batch short-seq traffic.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: routed LexiDocs traffic back to runtime-2.0.1 (confirmed reduced latency). Engineering rolled a hotfix to kernel-selector that adds a fast-path for sequences <128 tokens to prefer the lower-setup-cost kernel and skip JIT on initial invocations. Patch deployed to staging 2026-03-11 and to us-east-1 canary 2026-03-12.
Follow-ups: full rollout plan scheduled, add unit tests for kernel heuristics, add telemetry to detect high kernel-setup times and auto-fallback policy. Customer notified and provided post-incident runbook for pinning routing.
